issues.legal_issue: Statutory interest paid because compensation is deferred is a revenue receipt rather than part of the capital compensation.
material_facts: Compensation for the resumption of the jagir became due on the date of resumption, but was payable in annual instalments over a period of years.
The governing law separately provided for simple interest on the unpaid compensation until payment.
The assessee claimed that the interest formed part of the compensation and was a capital receipt; the tax authorities included it in income, while the Tribunal treated it as capital.
The High Court ruled against the assessee, and the assessee appealed.
issues.conclusion: The interest was a revenue receipt, distinct from the compensation, and was taxable as income; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 8(1) and 8(2) of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagir Act, 1951, compensation was determined under Schedule I and became due on resumption, while separately provided interest compensated the jagirdar for being kept out of the compensation until payment. The clear statutory use of “interest” bears its ordinary meaning and does not make the interest part of the capital compensation. The Court applied Dr. Sham Lal Narula v. Commissioner of Income-tax, 53 I.T.R. 151, which held that statutory interest under section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for delayed payment of compensation is a revenue receipt taxable under the Income-tax Act, 1922.

rule.if: income_tax_characterization_case and compensation_due_before_full_payment and compensation_paid_in_installments and separate_interest_paid_for_period_unpaid

predicates.income_tax_characterization_case: The proceeding concerns how a receipt is characterized for income-tax purposes.
predicates.compensation_due_before_full_payment: Compensation became due before the recipient received the full amount.
predicates.compensation_paid_in_installments: The compensation was paid in instalments rather than in full when it became due.
predicates.separate_interest_paid_for_period_unpaid: The payer separately paid interest to the recipient for the period the compensation remained unpaid.

issues.definition: When compensation is already due but paid in instalments and separate interest is paid for the unpaid period, that interest is treated as a taxable revenue receipt in an income-tax characterization case.

issues.legal_issue: A marginal heading cannot override the clear and unambiguous language of a statutory section.
material_facts: The section’s marginal heading described a duty to pay compensation.
The section’s operative language distinguished compensation, determined by specified principles and due on resumption, from interest payable until payment.
The assessee relied on the heading to argue that the interest formed part of the compensation.
issues.conclusion: The marginal heading could not control the interpretation of the section’s clear and unambiguous operative language.
issues.legal_principle: A marginal heading cannot control the words of a statutory section when those words are clear and unambiguous. The Court applied this principle in interpreting section 8 of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagir Act, 1951.

predicates.statutory_text_interpretation_case: The proceeding requires interpretation of statutory text.
predicates.marginal_heading_suggests_a_broader_mean: The marginal heading suggests a meaning broader than the operative text supports.
predicates.operative_text_is_clear_and_unambiguous: The operative text expresses its meaning clearly and unambiguously.

issues.definition: When a heading suggests a broader meaning than clear operative text supports, the heading does not control the text’s interpretation.
